t: Maximum Subarray Sum After at Most K Swaps — Window + Greedy Exchange
o: After up to k arbitrary swaps we want the best subarray sum. Key structural fact: an optimal solution takes some contiguous window W; each useful swap brings a large element from outside W into W in place of a small element inside W. So for each window, the answer is (window sum) + Σ over the best pairings of (largest outside values − smallest inside values), stopping when an outside value no longer exceeds an inside one. Example 2: window = whole array needs no swaps, sum 13. Example 1: window [1,0] gains 2−(−1)=3 via one swap.
k: Only contiguous windows matter: any optimal final subarray is a window, and swaps only shuttle values across its boundary.
Greedy exchange: pair the largest outside values with the smallest inside values, largest-with-smallest, while the outside value is strictly bigger.
Sliding the window with two ordered multisets lets us query the t-th smallest inside / t-th largest outside in O(log n).

a.i: For every window, copy the inside and outside values, sort them, and apply the greedy pairing. This directly mirrors the reasoning above and validates correctness, though it is cubic and only feasible on tiny inputs.
s: Sort inside ascending and outside descending.
Add gains a−b for paired values while a > b and at most k pairs; track the best total.
a.t: O(n³ log n) — O(n²) windows, each requiring sorting O(n log n)

a.n: Approach 2: Ordered multisets with incremental sliding (optimal)
a.i: Keep two sorted containers: `inside` (ascending) and `outside` (all other elements). Extending the right edge moves one element between them in O(log n); advancing the left edge moves one back. The greedy gain is read by indexing positions without mutating the containers, so each window is processed in O(k log n) after cheap updates.
s: Initialize outside with all elements, inside empty, window sum 0.
For each left, first eject nums[left−1] from inside (subtract from sum); then for each right, insert nums[right] into inside, remove from outside, add to sum.
Compute gain by scanning t = 0..k−1 comparing outside's (t+1)-th largest with inside's (t+1)-th smallest; stop when outside ≤ inside.
Update the answer with sum + gain for every window.

c.python:
from sortedcontainers import SortedList
class Solution:
    def maxSubarraySum(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        inside, outside = SortedList(), SortedList(nums)
        cur = 0
        best = float('-inf')
        for left in range(n):
            if left > 0:
                inside.remove(nums[left - 1])
                cur -= nums[left - 1]
            for right in range(left, n):
                x = nums[right]
                inside.add(x)
                outside.remove(x)
                cur += x
                gain = 0
                for t in range(min(k, len(inside), len(outside))):
                    a, b = outside[-1 - t], inside[t]
                    if a <= b:
                        break
                    gain += a - b
                best = max(best, cur + gain)
        return best

a.t: O(n² log n) — O(n²) window steps with O(log n) ordered-container updates; the gain scan is capped at k and breaks early

w: In an interview, state the "window + boundary exchanges" reduction first — it is the crux. Pitfalls: allowing swaps that hurt (only pair when outside > inside), forgetting k = 0 (plain Kadane-style answer, covered since gain = 0), duplicate values (use multisets/count maps, not sets), and 64-bit accumulation. Follow-up: can you avoid the O(k) scan per window with two heaps and lazy deletion, or handle "subarray after exactly k swaps"?
